Node and shape names survive string resolution
rows.evidence: crates/nvre-editor/examples/corpusresolve.rs, plus a fix in nvre-nif::scene::resolve_strings. FormIDs resolved: fnv 629,943/629,943, fo3 932,162/932,162, skyrim 1,161,479/1,161,479, skyrimse 1,188,909/1,188,909, fo4 2,197,903/2,197,903 — 0 unresolved in all five. The 5 FNV / 66 Skyrim LE / 72 Skyrim SE unnamed nodes held Bethesda's null-string sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF, which the string table has no entry for, so the name stayed the number 4294967295. Now resolved to the empty name, matching nifgen. Pinned by s2_5_the_null_string_index_resolves_to_the_empty_name.

rows.evidence: crates/nvre-editor/examples/geomsurvey.rs over each game's whole corpus (release build). fnv 2,255 one-UV and 1,177 no-UV of 67,174 shapes; fo3 1,716 and 1,116 of 57,218; skyrim 16 and 1,866 of 80,742; skyrimse 1,970 and 6,279 of 61,886; fo4 1,665 and 540,965 of 662,902. FO4's 540,965 are all under meshes\precombined, and they are correctly read: FO4 stores that geometry outside the NIF, in Fallout4 - Geometry.csg, keyed by a BSPackedGeomObject filename hash and offset. Format reverse-engineered and documented in docs/spec-notes/fo4-csg-format.md; the reader is not written yet.
